models.model_label: Primary FERC model: returns on earnings, future earnings/returns, smoothing, and smoothing interactions
models.sample_description: Firm-year observations from the 2004 version of Compustat's combined industrial annual data, for 1993–2000. Firms in financial and regulated industries (SIC 4000–4999 and 6000–6999) are excluded. The income-smoothing measure requires current-year and prior-four-year changes in discretionary accruals and pre-discretionary income. The primary test requires nonmissing earnings, operating cash flows, and accruals for past, current, and future three years, and returns for current and future three years. The authors trim observations in the top or bottom 1 percent of the stated distributions and remove extreme observations where earnings, operating cash flows, or total accruals in the past/current/future three years exceed 10 times or fall below −10 times market equity, or future three-year compound returns exceed 10 or fall below −10. The resulting primary-test sample is 17,019 firm-years. The accrual-construction fits use Compustat data from 1988–2000.
models.method_details: The authors describe Regression (4) as a pooled cross-sectional/time-series regression but do not name OLS or another underlying estimator.

review_notes: Source-first selection: Regression (4) is explicitly the primary empirical model, reported as Table 3 Panel C on the 17,019-observation full primary sample. Regression (5)/Panel A is expressly confirmatory; Regression (3)/Panel B is a CKSS benchmark; Panel D and later tests are an earnings decomposition and robustness extensions, so they are outside the selected principal family.

Income smoothing is the constructed measure used to answer the substantive information-versus-garbling question. The required fitted accrual construction is retained as a dependency; the deterministic five-observation correlation/rank itself requires no additional regression.
results_review_notes: Regression (4) is explicitly identified as the primary empirical model and is estimated on pooled cross-sectional/time-series data; the paper does not name OLS or another underlying estimator.
The ordinary intercept b0 and all nine frozen predictors are reported in Panel C. No additional Z controls are included in this selected primary model.
Adjusted R-squared 0.072 and N=17,019 are retained as auxiliary rows on the existing Table 3 Panel C fit.

models.model_label: Cross-sectional modified Jones model with ROA for discretionary accrual construction
models.sample_description: Compustat industry-year cross-sections from 1988–2000, grouped by two-digit SIC and year. The authors report 650 cross-sectional fits after excluding 110 cross-sections with fewer than 10 observations. Exact per-fit Ns and an aggregate observation count are not reported; each included fit has at least 10 observations. The study-level data section states that financial and regulated industries are excluded, but the construction-fit paragraph does not separately restate the sector filter.
models.method_details: The source describes a cross-sectional Jones model modified by Kothari et al. (2005), including ROA, but does not name the underlying estimator.

missing_fields.method: The source identifies a cross-sectional modified Jones model with ROA but does not state the underlying estimator.
missing_fields.sample_size: The source reports 650 usable industry-year fits after excluding 110 cross-sections below 10 observations; it does not report aggregate observations across fits or exact per-fit Ns. Each retained fit therefore has at least 10 observations, but the exact counts vary or are unreported.
missing_fields.sample_description: The study-level data section states that financial and regulated industries are excluded, but the construction-fit paragraph does not explicitly restate whether that sector filter applies to every 1988–2000 industry-year accrual fit.

review_notes: Regression (1) is retained only because its fit generates the discretionary-accrual residual DAP used in the primary model’s IS measure. The fitted values are NDAP and residuals are DAP; PDI is NI−DAP. The correlation/rank construction is deterministic and is not another fitted regression.
The inverse-assets term is a scaled constant regressor, distinct from an ordinary intercept. The source transcription confirms four RHS regressors and no separate ordinary intercept.
models.results_reason: Supporting-model results are outside this campaign.

review_notes: Source-first baseline choice: Regression (4), Table 3 Panel C, is the authors’ primary full-sample test of whether income smoothing improves the informativeness of current returns about future earnings. Regression (5)/Panel A is expressly confirmatory; Regression (3)/Panel B is a CKSS benchmark; Panel D and later specifications are decomposition/robustness tests and are excluded. The income-smoothing measure is developed to answer this substantive question, so it does not make the article a measurement-method paper.

The only indispensable fitted construction is modified Jones/Kothari Regression (1): residual DAP enters the rolling income-smoothing measure; fitted NDAP is used to define DAP; PDI=NI−DAP. The correlation and reversed fractional rank themselves are deterministic, so no other construction fit is included.
